# Benefits and responsibilities

Place alternatives in a shared composition using the benefits and responsibilities layout.

## Grouped model

[Model variants and named fields](../models/text-cards.md)

```latex
\studiotemplate[variant=two,palette=light]{text-cards}
```

Use the documented semantic fields or the lower-level numbered slots; replaced semantic names are not retained.

Numeric defaults and charts are illustrative.

## Layout options

| Option | Type | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `show-title` | boolean | `true` | Show the slide heading without moving panels. |
| `show-card-titles` | boolean | `true` | Show card headings or icon captions. |
| `show-card-bodies` | boolean | `true` | Show card descriptions. |
| `show-introduction` | boolean | `true` | Show the introduction in sidebar layouts; no effect elsewhere. |
| `show-icons` | boolean | `true` | Show original icons where present; no effect in text-only layouts. |

For example: `\studiotemplate[variant=two,show-title=false]{text-cards}`. Options are not text slots; invalid values produce an error.

## Typed content slots

Use `text/N` for text, `icon/N` for an icon name, `image/N` for an image path,
and `graphic/N` for LaTeX graphics. Numbers are local to this model and stored
in its metadata; the map below shows their positions. Supplied graphics are fitted
proportionally. Text fonts and alignment remain fixed.

Use `clear=text` to remove shipped copy before adding your own; option order does not matter.
Omitted fields keep their defaults. Named aliases such as `text/title` also work.

| Public slot | Existing field | Content and appearance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `icon/1`, `image/1`, `graphic/1` | `graphic-1` | Replaces this complete graphic; other elements stay fixed. |
| `icon/2`, `image/2`, `graphic/2` | `graphic-2` | Replaces this complete graphic; other elements stay fixed. |
| `text/1` | `title` | Main text |
| `text/2` | `text-2` | Editable text |
| `text/4` | `text-3` | Editable text |
| `text/3` | `text-4` | Editable text |
| `text/5` | `text-5` | Editable text |

Original unscoped field names remain compatible. For a labelled block, changing
`text/N` replaces the complete box; use `heading/N` and `body/N` for structured edits.

## Insert this slide

Place this command outside another `frame`:

```latex
\studiotemplate{benefits-limits}
```

## Change the content

This example uses supported fields. Omitted fields keep their shipped defaults.

```latex
\studiotemplate[
  text/1={Slide title},
  text/2={Supporting explanation}
]{benefits-limits}
```

## Complete one-slide example

Create `my-slide.tex` in the project root and paste:

```latex
\documentclass[aspectratio=169]{beamer}
\usetheme{bitpolito-studio}
\usepackage{bitpolitostudiotemplates}
\usepackage[backend=biber]{biblatex}
\addbibresource{bibliography.bib}
\begin{document}
\studiotemplate[
  text/1={Slide title},
  text/2={Supporting explanation}
]{benefits-limits}
\end{document}
```

```sh
python3 scripts/build.py my-slide.tex
# Installed TeX alternative:
python3 scripts/build.py my-slide.tex --backend native
```

Output: `build/my-slide.pdf`. On Windows use `py -3` instead of `python3`.

## Editable fields

Positions and available space refer to the original, fixed composition.
In the individual web view, select a field or enable **Show editable areas** to locate it.

| Field | What it changes | Position | Available space | Shipped value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <code>graphic-1</code> | Complete graphic, image or decoration (graphic) | middle left | 41.9% wide × 34.7% high | <code>\studiopaletteimage[width=805\studiounit]{images/studio/collection/figma-0064-part-01.pdf}</code> |
| <code>graphic-2</code> | Complete graphic, image or decoration (graphic) | middle right | 41.9% wide × 34.5% high | <code>\studiopaletteimage[width=805\studiounit]{images/studio/collection/figma-0064-part-02.pdf}</code> |
| <code>title</code> | Main text (text) | upper centre | 44.2% wide × 8.5% high | <code>Slide title</code> |
| <code>text-2</code> | Editable text (text) | middle left | 33.9% wide × 5.0% high | <code>Supporting explanation</code> |
| <code>text-3</code> | Editable text (text) | middle left | 33.9% wide × 16.8% high | <code>Supporting explanation.\\Add your own details.</code> |
| <code>text-4</code> | Editable text (text) | middle right | 32.1% wide × 5.6% high | <code>Supporting explanation</code> |
| <code>text-5</code> | Editable text (text) | middle right | 32.1% wide × 16.8% high | <code>Supporting explanation.\\Add your own details.</code> |

Truncated values are shown in full at the start of the current source file.
A text field accepts LaTeX; a graphic field accepts an icon, `\includegraphics`, TikZ or math.

## Replace a graphic

This example selects an icon by catalogue name; its size and position come from the slot:

```latex
\studiotemplate[
  icon/1={alice}
]{benefits-limits}
```

Use a numbered slot listed above to target another graphic. Some slots contain a complete
panel, background, screenshot or decoration. Inspect the preview before replacing them.

## Keep the composition

- Keep replacements within their allocated boxes. Shorten text or use explicit `\\` line breaks.
- Use `text/N={}` or `icon/N={}` to hide content while retaining its space; separated card panels stay visible.
- Fonts, anchors and geometry remain fixed; unknown fields and overflowing content produce diagnostics.
- Text colour does not recolour supplied graphics; prepare another asset when its fixed colours must change.
- Some diagrams, QR codes and decorations are native source elements rather than configurable fields.
- For structural changes, edit [the current source](../../../templates/studio/benefits-limits.tex). Catalogues and the showcase reuse it.
